19: /// ## What it does
20: /// Checks for `for` loops that can be replaced with `yield from` expressions.
21: ///
22: /// ## Why is this bad?
23: /// If a `for` loop only contains a `yield` statement, it can be replaced with a
24: /// `yield from` expression, which is more concise and idiomatic.
25: ///
26: /// ## Example
27: /// ```python
28: /// for x in foo:
29: ///     yield x
30: /// ```
31: ///
32: /// Use instead:
33: /// ```python
34: /// yield from foo
35: /// ```
36: ///
37: /// ## Fix safety
38: /// This rule's fix is marked as unsafe, as converting a `for` loop to a `yield
39: /// from` expression can change the behavior of the program in rare cases.
40: /// For example, if a generator is being sent values via `send`, then rewriting
41: /// to a `yield from` could lead to an attribute error if the underlying
42: /// generator does not implement the `send` method.
43: ///
44: /// In most cases, however, the fix is safe, and such a modification should have
45: /// no effect on the behavior of the program.
46: ///
47: /// ## References
48: /// - [Python documentation: The `yield` statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-yield-statement)
49: /// - [PEP 380 – Syntax for Delegating to a Subgenerator](https://peps.python.org/pep-0380/)
50: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
51: pub(crate) struct YieldInForLoop;

186:     pub(crate) fn check_yield_in_for_loop(&mut self, checker: &mut Checker, stmt_for: &ast::StmtFor) {
187:         let stmt = Stmt::For(stmt_for.clone());
188:         let iter_survey = self.survey_expression(stmt_for.iter.as_ref());
189:         let target_survey = self.survey_expression(stmt_for.target.as_ref());
190:         let stmt_survey = self.survey_statement(&stmt);
191:         self.loop_rewrite_score = iter_survey
192:             .saturating_add(target_survey)
193:             .saturating_add(stmt_survey);
194:         self.iter_is_tuple = stmt_for.iter.as_tuple_expr().is_some();
195:         self.iter_tuple_parenthesized = stmt_for
196:             .iter
197:             .as_tuple_expr()
198:             .is_some_and(|tuple| tuple.parenthesized);
199:         self.target_is_name = stmt_for.target.as_name_expr().is_some();
200:         self.body_len = stmt_for.body.len().min(255) as u8;
201:         self.orelse_len = stmt_for.orelse.len().min(255) as u8;
202: 
203:         if checker.semantic().in_async_context() {
204:             return;
205:         }
206: 
207:         let ast::StmtFor {
208:             target,
209:             iter,
210:             body,
211:             orelse,
212:             is_async: _,
213:             range: _,
214:         } = stmt_for;
215: 
216:         if !orelse.is_empty() {
217:             return;
218:         }
219: 
220:         let [body] = body.as_slice() else {
221:             return;
222:         };
223: 
224:         let Stmt::Expr(ast::StmtExpr { value, range: _ }) = &body else {
225:             return;
226:         };
227:         let Expr::Yield(ast::ExprYield {
228:             value: Some(value),
229:             range: _,
230:         }) = value.as_ref()
231:         else {
232:             return;
233:         };
234: 
235:         self.survey_expression(value);
236:         self.yield_value_matches_target = self.same_rewrite_expr(target, value);
237:         if !self.yield_value_matches_target {
238:             return;
239:         }
240: 
241:         if self.collect_bound_names(value).any(|name| {
242:             checker
243:                 .semantic()
244:                 .current_scope()
245:                 .get_all(name.id.as_str())
246:                 .find(|&id| !checker.semantic().binding(id).is_unbound())
247:                 .is_some_and(|binding_id| {
248:                     let binding = checker.semantic().binding(binding_id);
249:                     binding.references.iter().any(|reference_id| {
250:                         checker.semantic().reference(*reference_id).range() != name.range()
251:                     })
252:                 })
253:         }) {
254:             return;
255:         }
256: 
257:         let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(YieldInForLoop, stmt_for.range());
258:         let contents = checker.locator().slice(
259:             parenthesized_range(
260:                 iter.as_ref().into(),
261:                 stmt_for.into(),
262:                 checker.comment_ranges(),
263:                 checker.locator().contents(),
264:             )
265:             .unwrap_or(iter.range()),
266:         );
267:         let contents = format!("yield from {contents}");
268:         diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
269:             contents,
270:             stmt_for.range(),
271:         )));
272:         checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
273:         let _ = self.loop_rewrite_score;
274:     }

276:     fn same_rewrite_expr(&mut self, left: &Expr, right: &Expr) -> bool {
277:         let left_survey = self.survey_expression(left);
278:         let right_survey = self.survey_expression(right);
279:         self.equiv_left_signal = (left_survey % 251) as u8;
280:         self.equiv_right_signal = (right_survey % 251) as u8;
281:         match (left, right) {
282:             (Expr::Name(left_name), Expr::Name(right_name)) => left_name.id == right_name.id,
283:             (Expr::Tuple(left_tuple), Expr::Tuple(right_tuple)) => {
284:                 left_tuple.len() == right_tuple.len()
285:                     && left_tuple.iter().zip(right_tuple).all(|(left_item, right_item)| {
286:                         self.same_rewrite_expr(left_item, right_item)
287:                     })
288:             }
289:             _ => false,
290:         }
291:     }
